paras: The expulsion of Black section hands near Corsicana, Texas, took place in August 1903, when Black men working on a section in the neighborhood were ordered to quit the vicinity. A telegraph brief gave their alleged thefts as the reason and said that they left; neither report named who gave the order.

On August 24, 1903, the San Antonio Daily Light carried a one-line item reporting that "Negro section hands near Corsicana" had been "ordered to quit the vicinity, on account of their thefts, and they leave." The item did not say how many men were involved, who accused them, or who ordered them out. No violence against the workers was reported.

A Corsicana dispatch dated August 28 placed the workers more precisely, in the neighborhood of Angus, about five miles south of the city. That dispatch concerned a different incident, in which a Black man was said to have entered the house of a widow named Wilson near Angus and awakened Miss Lutie Wilson before escaping through a window. Its last sentence noted that "Negroes working on the section in this neighborhood were ordered to leave a short time ago," without giving a reason or stating any link to the intrusion.
No report of arrests, an investigation, or any official response to the order appears in the coverage, and no account says where the workers went.

Coverage was slight and came only from white Texas papers. The San Antonio Daily Light listed the expulsion among its "Telegraph Brevities," between items on fighting in Macedonia and a railroad damage suit, and repeated the thefts charge without attribution. The Bryan Morning Eagle, under the headline "Entered Room," mentioned the order only at the close of its account of the Wilson intrusion, so that the two items appeared side by side without comment. No Black-press report of the expulsion was found.
